definitions.explanation: Thin shavings of dried, fermented, and smoked skipjack tuna, used for making dashi and as a topping.

examples.japanese: {鰹節|かつおぶし}を{削|けず}る。
examples.notes: Traditional preparation involves shaving from a block

examples.japanese: お{好|この}み{焼|や}きの{上|うえ}に{鰹節|かつおぶし}をかける。
examples.english: Sprinkle bonito flakes on top of okonomiyaki.

examples.japanese: {鰹節|かつおぶし}と{昆布|こんぶ}で{合|あ}わせ{出汁|だし}を{作|つく}る。
examples.english: Make combined dashi from bonito flakes and kelp.

notes:
One of the hardest natural foods in the world. The fermentation process can take months. Types:
- {荒節|あらぶし} (arabushi) - basic dried/smoked bonito
- {枯節|かれぶし} (karebushi) - mold-fermented, higher quality
- {本枯節|ほんかれぶし} (honkarebushi) - multiple fermentations, premium

Forms available:
- {削|けず}り{節|ぶし} (pre-shaved flakes)
- {糸|いと}{削|けず}り (fine threads)
- {厚|あつ}{削|けず}り (thick shavings for dashi)

The flakes 'dance' ({踊|おど}る) when placed on hot food due to heat convection.
